overall: The AG found the Cape Light Compact did not violate the Open Meeting Law: its executive session topic statement was specific enough, and invoking Purpose 10 for competitively sensitive power supply information was proper.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Compact failed to adequately disclose the topics for its November 12, 2014 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that this level of detail was sufficient to inform the public of the subjects of the executive session discussion, as required by G.L. c. 30A, § 21(b)(3).

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Compact entered executive session for an improper purpose, namely invoking Purpose 10 to discuss power supply matters.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the CLC did not violate the Open Meeting Law by invoking Purpose 10 as the basis for its November 12, 2014 executive session.
